topic: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: a 24B MoE that runs like a 2B
thesis: LiquidAI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B keeps 24B parameters in memory but computes each token with only 2.45B of them, so a laptop runs a 24B model at small-model speed -- 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max.
explanation_path: Start from the one distinction the whole video hangs on: a model's total parameter count is what memory pays for, while its active parameter count is what speed pays for; establish that before any product name appears. Then walk one token through the model: 24.0B parameters stored, a router inside each mixture-of-experts block paging 4 of 64 experts, 2.45B parameters actually computing. Only then land the measured payoff -- 184 tokens per second decode on an Apple M5 Max using 15 GB of memory at Q4_K_M -- and immediately follow with the honest catch: all 24B still sit in memory, knowledge-heavy benchmarks go to the bigger Qwen (the vendor's own table says so), and Ollama's lfm2.5 tag today pulls the 8B model, so the real day-one command is the llama.cpp one-liner.

claims.claim: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device; it is the largest and final model in the LFM2.5 family.
claims.source_title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for Fast On-Device Agents (Liquid AI blog)

claims.claim: The announcement is dated October 13, 2026, and both the base and post-trained models are open-weight on Hugging Face.
claims.source_title: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B (Hugging Face blog)

claims.claim: The model card's spec list gives 24.0B total parameters and 2.45B active parameters per token.

The architecture has 40 layers (30 double-gated short convolution blocks plus 10 GQA), 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and a 131,072-token context window, extended from the predecessor's 32,768.

Day-one runtimes are Transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, MLX and LM Studio (plus ONNX and FP8 checkpoints); on MLX you must install mlx-lm>=0.32.0 because earlier versions route the experts incorrectly.

At Q4_K_M with llama.cpp it decodes 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max and 114 tokens/s on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, up to 1.7x faster than the next comparable MoE, while using the least memory of the compared models (15 GB on the M5 Max, 4K-token input context).
claims.source_title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for Fast On-Device Agents (Liquid AI blog)

claims.claim: On Liquid's own 16-benchmark table it is competitive with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a model with ~50% more total and active parameters, leading on five of eight agentic and tool-use benchmarks: LiveClaw 48.09 versus 38.19 and AutomationBench 27.69 versus 8.72 (all evals run with vLLM by Liquid AI).
claims.source_title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for Fast On-Device Agents (Liquid AI blog)

claims.claim: The same table shows where it loses: GPQA Diamond 74.42 versus Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's 83.69, and SWE-Bench Verified (OpenCode) 51.00 versus 66.20; Liquid itself recommends pairing it with retrieval or web search for knowledge-heavy work.
claims.source_title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for Fast On-Device Agents (Liquid AI blog)

claims.claim: The official GGUF repo lists a 14.5 GB Q4_K_M build and a 13.6 GB Q4_0 build that is a Quantization-Aware Distillation checkpoint trained to recover accuracy lost to quantization; the repo showed 17,807 downloads in its first day, and runs with one llama.cpp line.

Ollama's lfm2.5 tag list, fetched on 2026-10-14, contains only the 8B family -- five tags, all of them 8b-a1b variants at 5.2 GB to 17 GB -- so 'ollama run lfm2.5' does not get you this 24B model yet.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: A specialist clinic with 64 doctors where a triage nurse pages exactly 4 per patient visit
analogy_candidates.mapping: The full roster (24B parameters) is on staff and paid for in memory, but each visit (each token) is handled by just the 4 specialists paged (2.45B active parameters), so visits are fast while the expertise on call is huge.
analogy_candidates.limit: The clinic pays all 64 salaries whether or not they are paged -- RAM cost never shrinks with activity -- and it hides that the nurse (the router) takes a small cut of every single visit.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: A tradesperson's van carrying the full tool inventory, where each job touches only a few tools
analogy_candidates.mapping: The van is the 14.5 GB Q4_K_M download holding all 24B parameters; you haul the whole kit so any specialty is on hand, but a given job moves at small-kit speed.
analogy_candidates.limit: A van does not choose its own tools -- the model's router scores and picks experts fresh for every token, and different tokens pick different tools, which the van image flattens out.

misconceptions.myth: A 24B model is out of reach for a laptop; big model always means big, slow inference.
misconceptions.reality: Memory does hold all 24B (a 14.5 GB Q4_K_M download, 15 GB in use on an M5 Max), but each token computes through only 2.45B parameters, so decode speed tracks a small model -- 184 tokens/s measured with llama.cpp (claims 3 and 6).

misconceptions.myth: If only about 2B parameters are active, it must think like a 2B model; the 24B is marketing.
misconceptions.reality: Capacity is stored across 64 experts per MoE block and selected per token (claim 4); it beats the bigger Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 5 of 8 agentic benchmarks (claim 7) while losing GPQA Diamond and SWE-Bench (claim 8) -- the win is agent skill and speed, not encyclopedic knowledge.

glossary.definition: A learned number inside a model; more parameters usually means more capability, and always means more memory.
A model design that stores many specialist sub-networks and, for each token, activates only the few a gatekeeper picks.
One specialist sub-network inside the model; LFM2.5-24B-A2B has 64 to choose from in each MoE block.
The subset of the model's parameters that actually compute on a given token -- here 2.45B out of 24.0B.
The small network that scores all experts and picks which 4 handle each token.
A chunk of text roughly a word long; models read and write one token at a time.
How fast a model generates text; higher means snappier replies.
Storing model weights in fewer bits to shrink memory; here it turns 24B parameters into a 14.5 GB file.
The single-file format that llama.cpp-based tools load; one download is the whole model.
A model that writes an explicit chain of thought before its final answer; this one always does.

unverified: Community reception threads on r/LocalLLaMA and r/LocalLLM returned 403 this session, so any community-reported tokens-per-second figures or quality impressions are unverified.
The Hugging Face trending rank of 234 and the like counts come from the stage-02 idea note, not from a page fetched this session.

Tokens per second on our own DGX Spark and consumer GPUs is not yet measured; the only fetched numbers are Liquid's (Apple M5 Max 184 tok/s, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 114 tok/s, both llama.cpp at Q4_K_M).
Artificial Analysis has not evaluated LFM2.5-24B-A2B itself; whether independent testers rate its intelligence above the predecessor's is unknown.
An Ollama tag for LFM2.5-24B-A2B may appear after this brief is written; the gap was verified only on 2026-10-14.
suggested_outline:
Open on the impossible-sounding number: a 24B-parameter model decoded at 184 tokens per second on a laptop, because 21.55B of those parameters never touched that token.
One scenario carries the explanation: follow a single token through the clinic -- the router pages 4 of 64 specialists per block, 2.45B parameters fire, the other 21.55B wait their turn; total parameters are what memory pays for, active parameters are what speed pays for.
The honest catch, said plainly: all 24B still sit in memory (15 GB at Q4_K_M), it loses GPQA Diamond and SWE-Bench to the bigger Qwen, and Ollama's lfm2.5 tag is still the 8B -- so the real day-one move is the llama.cpp one-liner on a 14.5 GB download.
notes: All benchmark, speed and memory numbers are vendor-run (Liquid AI, evaluated with vLLM; edge metrics via llama.cpp Q4_K_M on Pipette) and should be attributed to Liquid on camera. Artificial Analysis has only the predecessor LFM2-24B-A2B: 23.8B total and 2.3B active parameters, rated 6 (estimated) on the AA Intelligence Index and described as below average in intelligence among similar open-weight non-reasoning models -- a reason to hedge quality claims for the new model until independent numbers exist. Ollama's lfm2:24b-a2b tag (23.8B params, Q4_K_M 14 GB, 1.1M downloads, updated 7 months ago) is the older LFM2-24B-A2B, not this release; do not show it as the way to run LFM2.5. The model card sidebar showed 4,067 downloads within the first day. API price on Liquid Console: $.10/1M input tokens (at $.05 for cached input) and $1.00/1M output tokens. MLX users need mlx-lm>=0.32.0; earlier versions route the experts incorrectly.
viewer_situation: You run models at home in Ollama or LM Studio on a 16-to-32 GB Mac or gaming PC, you have watched small models fly and 24B-class models crawl, and you just saw 'a 24B MoE that runs like a 2B' start trending on Hugging Face.
objection: All 24B parameters still have to sit in memory (15 GB even at 4-bit), and 2.45B active genuinely caps depth -- it lost GPQA Diamond 74.42 to 83.69 and SWE-Bench 51.00 to 66.20 against the bigger Qwen3.6-35B-A3B -- so you are trading some of what it knows for how fast it moves.
